title: Integration: edit mode, save sync, dirty tabs, documentation

tasks.title: Add Edit mode, save, revision guard and draft handling to the file viewer
tasks.detail:
Goal: Make a text file editable in place with the CodeMirror `FileEditor`, save it through `PUT`, keep the buffer alive across tab switches, and never auto-overwrite a dirty buffer.
Files: `components/FileViewer.tsx`, `lib/file-viewer-state.ts`, `components/FileViewer.test.mjs`. Do not touch `components/FileEditor.tsx`, `components/file-tab-state.ts`, `components/AppShell.tsx`, `components/TabBar.tsx`, or any i18n file.
Contract (all four phases of the previous foundation work are already merged):
- `lib/file-viewer-state.ts`: `export type FileViewerDisplayMode = "source" | "preview" | "diff" | "edit";` and `FileViewerState` gains `draft?: string | null`. `resolveInitialFileDisplayMode` keeps returning `"source"` by default.
- `FileData` gains `revision: string` (the server returns it in the text `read` response).
- `getFileApiUrl`'s `type` parameter union gains `"write"`; the resulting URL is `/api/files/<encoded>?type=write` and the server ignores that query parameter for `PUT`.
- `DISPLAY_MODE_LABELS` gains `edit: "Edit"` (the `Record<DisplayMode, string>` type forces this).
- `Props` gains `onDirtyChange?: (dirty: boolean) => void` (optional, so `AppShell` can adopt it in TASK-009).
Behaviour:
1. `const canEdit = !data?.truncated && !isDeletedDiff;` declared **before** `effectiveDisplayMode`. `displayModes` always includes `"edit"` so the control stays discoverable, but the Edit button is `disabled={!canEdit}` with `title`/`aria-label` set to `t("i18n.fileTooLargeToEdit")` when `!canEdit` and `t("i18n.edit")` otherwise. `effectiveDisplayMode` must fall back so a file that becomes un-editable while edit mode is selected can never render the editor: `const effectiveDisplayMode = isDeletedDiff ? "diff" : (!canEdit && displayMode === "edit" ? "source" : displayMode);`
2. Buffer state: `editorValue` (`useState`), `dirty` (`useState`), plus refs `editorValueRef`, `dirtyRef`, `savingRef`, `revisionRef`, `eolRef: "\n" | "\r\n"`, `loadedTextRef` (the LF-normalized disk text the buffer was based on).
3. On identity change and after `fetchContent` resolves, call a local `applyDiskContent(content, revision)`: set `revisionRef.current = revision`; if `content.includes("\r\n")` set `eolRef.current = "\r\n"`; set `loadedTextRef.current = content.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n")`; if `initialState?.draft != null` set `editorValue` to the draft and `dirty = true` (a restored draft wins over disk), otherwise set `editorValue = loadedTextRef.current` and `dirty = false`; mirror both into `viewerStateRef.current.draft` and call `onDirtyChange`.
4. `handleEditorChange(next)`: set `editorValue`/`editorValueRef`; `const isDirty = next !== loadedTextRef.current`; set `dirty`/`dirtyRef`; `viewerStateRef.current.draft = isDirty ? next : null`; `onDirtyChangeRef.current?.(isDirty)`. The unmount cleanup that already calls `onStateChange({ ...viewerStateRef.current })` therefore persists the draft, which is what makes an unsaved buffer survive a tab switch (only the active tab mounts a `FileViewer`).
5. `saveFile()`: guard on `savingRef.current`; send `fetch(getFileApiUrl(filePath, "write", sourceSessionId), { method: "PUT", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ content, baseRevision: revisionRef.current }) })` where `content = eolRef.current === "\r\n" ? editorValueRef.current.replace(/\n/g, "\r\n") : editorValueRef.current`. On `200`: read the JSON, set `revisionRef.current`, `loadedTextRef.current = editorValueRef.current`, `dirty = false`, `viewerStateRef.current.draft = null`, `onDirtyChange?.(false)`, clear any banner and show `i18n.saved`. On `409`: set a `"stale"` banner. On other failures: show `i18n.saveFailed` with the response error text.
6. Banner above the content area (next to the existing `data?.truncated` block), shown only when a banner state is set: `i18n.fileChangedOnDisk` + `i18n.reloadFromDisk` + `i18n.overwrite` for `"stale"`; `i18n.externalChangeDetected` + `i18n.reloadFromDisk` for `"external"`. Reload re-runs `fetchContent` and `applyDiskContent` (discarding the draft and clearing the draft from `viewerStateRef`); Overwrite re-reads the current revision with a plain `fetchContent` (updating only `revisionRef`), then calls `saveFile()` again.
7. SSE `change` in the existing watch effect: `fetchGitDiff` always runs; the content refresh must be gated — `if (dirtyRef.current) { setBanner("external"); } else { void fetchContent(filePath).then((d) => { if (d) applyDiskContent(d.content, d.revision); }); }`. This is the single change that makes save-based sync safe: a save in another tab or a write by the agent refreshes a clean viewer and never clobbers a dirty one.
8. Content area: when `effectiveDisplayMode === "edit"` render `<FileEditor value={editorValue} language={language} wrapLines={wrapLines} onChange={handleEditorChange} onSave={() => void saveFile()} />` and nothing else; the syntax-highlighter and lightweight branches must not render in that mode. `useLightweightSource` must be false when `effectiveDisplayMode === "edit"`.
9. Toolbar: when `effectiveDisplayMode === "edit"`, add a save button in `file-viewer-actions` labelled `i18n.saveFile` / `i18n.saving` / `i18n.saved`, disabled unless `dirty`, plus a small dirty indicator reusing the existing `file-viewer-live-indicator` styling whose `title` and `aria-label` are `t("i18n.unsavedChanges")`.
Trap to respect: `components/FileViewer.test.mjs` (line 41) extracts a fixed list of variable declarations (`viewerContent`, `sourceLines`, `language`, `isHtml`, `isMarkdown`, `hasPreview`, `effectiveDisplayMode`, `useLightweightSource`, `lightweightSourceLines`) and evaluates them in a synthetic function. `effectiveDisplayMode` and `useLightweightSource` now reference `canEdit`, so that extraction list must be extended with `"canEdit"` in the same edit, and `canEdit` must be declared before `effectiveDisplayMode` so the sliced declarations keep their order. Gate `useLightweightSource` on `!(effectiveDisplayMode === "edit")` so the syntax highlighter never builds in edit mode.
Steps:
1. Extend `lib/file-viewer-state.ts` and `FileData`/`getFileApiUrl`/`DISPLAY_MODE_LABELS` exactly as specified.
2. Implement the buffer, save, banner, dirty-guard and edit branch in `TextFileViewer`.
3. Extend `components/FileViewer.test.mjs` with source assertions: `"edit"` appears in the `FileViewerDisplayMode` union and in `DISPLAY_MODE_LABELS`; the Edit button is `disabled={!canEdit}` with an `i18n.fileTooLargeToEdit` tooltip and `effectiveDisplayMode` falls back to `"source"` when `!canEdit`; the save call uses `method: "PUT"` and a `baseRevision` in the body; the watch `synchronize` path checks `dirtyRef.current` before calling `fetchContent`; `viewerStateRef.current.draft` is assigned on change and cleared on save; `<FileEditor` appears only in the edit branch.
Verify: `node --experimental-strip-types --test components/FileViewer.test.mjs` passes, `npm test` still passes, `node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` is clean, `npm run lint` is clean.
Done when: a clean text file can be edited and saved from the viewer, a dirty file is never auto-reloaded, a reloaded/overwritten conflict is reachable, the draft is stored in the viewer state, and all tests/type/lint gates pass.

tasks.title: Mark dirty file tabs and confirm before closing them
tasks.detail:
Goal: Surface an unsaved file-tab draft in the tab bar and stop a close from silently discarding it.
Files: `components/AppShell.tsx`, `components/TabBar.tsx`, `components/file-tab-state.ts`, `components/file-tab-state.test.mjs`, and a new `components/AppShell.file-editor.test.mjs`. Do not touch `components/FileViewer.tsx`, `components/FileEditor.tsx`, or any i18n file.
Contract: `FileViewer` already accepts the optional `onDirtyChange?: (dirty: boolean) => void` added by TASK-008, and `lib/file-viewer-state.ts` already has `draft?: string | null` inside `FileViewerState`.
1. `components/TabBar.tsx`: the `Tab` interface gains `dirty?: boolean`. Render, immediately before the tab label, `<span className="tab-dirty-dot" aria-hidden="true" />` when `tab.dirty`, using an inline `style` object (a 6px circle in `var(--accent)`) so no CSS file is touched. Do not change close/select behaviour.
2. `components/AppShell.tsx`:
   - `const [dirtyFileTabs, setDirtyFileTabs] = useState<Set<string>>(new Set());`
   - `const handleFileDirtyChange = useCallback((tabId: string, dirty: boolean) => { setDirtyFileTabs((prev) => { const next = new Set(prev); if (dirty) next.add(tabId); else next.delete(tabId); return next; }); }, []);`
   - Pass `onDirtyChange={(dirty) => handleFileDirtyChange(activeFileTab.id, dirty)}` to the mounted `<FileViewer>` in the file-content block.
   - Where the panel tab list is built (`const panelTabs: Tab[] = [...fileTabs, ...webPanelTabs.map(...)]`), map the file tabs to include `dirty: dirtyFileTabs.has(tab.id)`.
   - `handleCloseFileTab`: for a file tab whose id is in `dirtyFileTabs`, return early unless `window.confirm(translate("i18n.discardUnsavedChanges"))`; then delete the id from `dirtyFileTabs`. Use `translate` (the identifier AppShell already uses), not `t`. Terminal/web-panel branches stay unchanged. Do not add a confirmation on tab *switch* — the draft is already preserved through `viewerState.draft`.
3. `components/file-tab-state.ts`: in `openFileTab`, the branch that rebuilds `viewerState` for an existing tab with a `modeHint` must carry the draft: `draft: tab.viewerState?.draft ?? null`. The new-tab branch and the unchanged-tab early return stay as they are.
Steps:
1. Extend `TabBar.tsx` (type + dot) and `AppShell.tsx` (state, wiring, close confirmation).
2. Extend `components/file-tab-state.test.mjs` with a test that `openFileTab` with a `modeHint` on a tab whose `viewerState.draft` is `"unsaved text"` yields `viewerState.draft === "unsaved text"` while resetting `displayMode` and scroll to `0`.
3. Write `components/AppShell.file-editor.test.mjs` in the source-assertion style of `components/AppShell.file-viewer-state.test.mjs`: assert the mounted `FileViewer` receives `onDirtyChange`, the panel tab list marks file tabs with `dirty: dirtyFileTabs.has(`, `handleCloseFileTab` calls `window.confirm(translate("i18n.discardUnsavedChanges"))` before filtering the tab out, and `TabBar.tsx` renders `className="tab-dirty-dot"` behind `tab.dirty`.
Verify: `node --experimental-strip-types --test components/file-tab-state.test.mjs components/AppShell.file-editor.test.mjs` passes, `npm test` passes, `node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint` are clean.
Done when: editing a file shows a dot on its tab, closing that tab prompts, cancelling keeps the tab and draft, and a tab switch preserves the draft.

tasks.title: Record the decision in an ADR
tasks.detail:
Goal: Document why the editor is save-based, what the write endpoint guarantees, and which limits were accepted deliberately.
Files: create `docs/adr/0006-file-editor-save-sync.md` only.
Contract: follow the structure and tone of `docs/adr/0002-chat-only-tool-selection.md` through `docs/adr/0005-built-in-subagent-disable.md` (title, Status, Context, Decision, Alternatives considered, Consequences). Required content:
- Status: Accepted. Date 2026-10-02.
- Context: the file viewer was read-only by design; `/api/files/[...path]` had no write method; `fs.watch` on the target directory plus SSE already provided live change detection; the agent frequently writes the same files the user browses.
- Decision: add `PUT /api/files/[...path]` with an origin check, JSON content-type check, allowed-root + realpath containment, symlink refusal, a 1 MiB body cap, NUL rejection, and a `baseRevision` compare that answers `409`; write atomically while preserving permission bits; expose a `revision` token in the text read response; make `Edit` a fourth display mode backed by CodeMirror 6; gate the SSE content refresh on a clean buffer; keep an unsaved draft inside `FileViewerState.draft`; and preserve CRLF line endings across the round trip.
- Explicitly state that save-based sync is chosen over live keystroke collaboration, and explain why: the watcher is directory-scoped so the save already fans out to every tab, the writer's own echo is harmless because the incoming text equals the buffer, and OT/CRDT plus an upstream channel would be a much larger change for a single-operator, loopback-bound server.
- Alternatives considered and rejected: a plain `textarea` (no highlighting, loses parity with Source mode); `@codemirror/legacy-modes` for the long tail (extra dependency, and unknown modes were not worth the risk — those languages stay plain text but editable); writing with `writePrivateFileAtomicSync` (its `0o600` mode would rewrite source-file permissions); direct `fs.writeFileSync` (partial writes on crash); authorizing writes through `isFilePathReferencedBySession` (that path exists so a session can read outside the allowed roots, not write).
- Consequences and limits: files above `TEXT_PREVIEW_MAX_BYTES` (256 KiB) are not editable; only languages with an official `@codemirror/lang-*` package are highlighted; no file creation; no multi-user cursors; `Edit` is unavailable for deleted diffs.
Steps:
1. Write the ADR with the sections above.
2. Cross-reference `docs/adr/0002-chat-only-tool-selection.md` where the tool-preset precedent is relevant.
Verify: `ls docs/adr/0006-file-editor-save-sync.md` exists and the file contains an `Accepted` status, a `Context` section, a `Decision` section, `Alternatives considered`, and `Consequences`.
Done when: the ADR states the invariants an implementer must not break (no symlink writes, no unauthenticated writes, no dirty-buffer clobber) without restating the whole plan.

tasks.title: Verify the integrated editor end to end and report evidence
tasks.detail:
Goal: Prove the integrated feature satisfies the acceptance criteria, with raw evidence, before the plan is declared done.
Files: no file ownership; do not modify source. Record findings in `progress`; report defects instead of fixing them.
Steps:
1. Run `npm test`, `node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`, and `npm run lint`; capture pass/fail counts and any diagnostics.
2. Reuse the already-running dev server at `http://127.0.0.1:30141` (it is this checkout's `next dev`). Do **not** start a second `next dev`, do not run `next build`, and do not move `.next`.
3. Browser step 1: open a small text file in the right panel from the file explorer, switch to `Edit`, change one line, press `Mod-s`. Expect the toolbar to report the save and the file's git diff to appear.
4. Browser step 2 (save-based sync): open a second browser page (or tab) on the same URL, open the same file, then save in the first page. Expect the second page to show the new content without a manual refresh — this is the acceptance criterion for "save syncs everything".
5. Browser step 3 (external write, clean buffer): with a file open in `Source` mode, append a line with `printf 'x\n' >> <file>` and confirm the viewer refreshes.
6. Browser step 4 (conflict guard): open a file, type in `Edit` without saving, append to the file on disk, and confirm the "file changed on disk" banner appears while the typed text stays. Then press save and confirm the stale path is offered (`reload from disk` / `overwrite`) instead of a silent overwrite.
7. Browser step 5 (draft across tabs): with unsaved edits, switch to another file tab and back; confirm the edits are still there. Then close the dirty tab and confirm the discard prompt appears and that cancelling keeps the tab.
8. Browser step 6 (size limit): open a file larger than 256 KiB and confirm `Edit` is not offered.
9. Confirm the fork is undisturbed: `git status --porcelain` must not list `lib/rpc-manager.ts` or `lib/pi-types.ts`.
10. Record in `progress`: exact commands, observed results, any browser console errors, and any step that could not be reproduced.
Verify: the three commands pass; steps 3-8 behave as described; the evidence is recorded verbatim in `progress`.
Done when: every acceptance criterion in `plan.md` section 9 is either demonstrated with evidence or reported as a failure with the exact reproduction, and no source file was modified by this task.
